title: Energy in reactions - 123 school
heading: Energy in reactions
intro: Choose the correct answer for each question. Where BINAS is mentioned, look up the data in the table named. Use a calculator where needed.

questions.question: What does it mean if a reaction is exothermic?

answers.a: the reaction needs no activation energy

questions.question: A reaction has a heat of reaction of +1.5·10<sup>5</sup> J. What holds?

answers.a: the reaction does not take place

questions.question: When a substance dissolves in water the temperature drops. What is the dissolving?
In which BINAS table do you find the heats of formation of inorganic substances?
What is the heat of formation of H<sub>2</sub>O(l)? (BINAS table 57A)
What is the heat of formation of Cl<sub>2</sub>(g)?
Which formula gives the heat of reaction from heats of formation?

answers.a: Σ heat of formation of products + Σ heat of formation of starting substances
answers.b: Σ heat of formation of products – Σ heat of formation of starting substances
answers.c: Σ heat of formation of products × Σ heat of formation of starting substances
answers.d: Σ heat of formation of starting substances – Σ heat of formation of products

Calculate the heat of reaction of CaCO<sub>3</sub> → CaO + CO<sub>2</sub> (BINAS table 57A)
Is the decomposition of CaCO<sub>3</sub> into CaO and CO<sub>2</sub> exothermic or endothermic? (BINAS table 57A)
Calculate the heat of reaction of CaO + H<sub>2</sub>O(l) → Ca(OH)<sub>2</sub> (BINAS table 57A)
Calculate the heat of reaction of 2 SO<sub>2</sub> + O<sub>2</sub> → 2 SO<sub>3</sub> (all gaseous; BINAS table 57A)
Calculate the heat of reaction of 2 NO → N<sub>2</sub> + O<sub>2</sub> (BINAS table 57A)
Calculate the heat of reaction of Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> + 3 CO → 2 Fe + 3 CO<sub>2</sub> (BINAS table 57A)
The heat of formation of water is –2.86·10<sup>5</sup> J/mol. What is the heat of reaction of 2 H<sub>2</sub>O(l) → 2 H<sub>2</sub> + O<sub>2</sub>?
What is the heat of combustion of ethanol(l)? (BINAS table 56)
Calculate the reaction heat of CH<sub>4</sub> + 2 O<sub>2</sub> → CO<sub>2</sub> + 2 H<sub>2</sub>O(l). Use BINAS table 57A and for CH<sub>4</sub>(g) –0.75·10<sup>5</sup> J/mol (table 57B)
How much heat is released when 10 g of methane burns? (M = 16.04 g/mol; BINAS table 56)
What is activation energy?

answers.b: the energy released in the reaction
answers.c: the difference in energy between products and starting substances
answers.d: the minimum energy needed to start a reaction

questions.question: What happens to the activation energy if you add a catalyst?
What happens to the heat of reaction if you add a catalyst?
In an energy diagram the products lie higher than the starting substances. What is the reaction?
What is the activation energy in an energy diagram?

answers.a: the difference between the products and the starting substances
answers.b: the difference between the top and the level of the starting substances

questions.question: Why is a reaction faster at a higher temperature?

answers.b: more collisions have enough energy to react
answers.c: the heat of reaction becomes larger

questions.question: What takes energy in a reaction?

answers.c: breaking bonds in the starting substances

questions.question: Methane and oxygen do not react without a spark, even though the reaction is exothermic. What is the reason?

answers.a: the heat of reaction is zero
answers.c: the activation energy must first be supplied
